Abiel
AY-bee-el
proper noun
Hebrew Avi’el, “God is my father” or “my father is God,” the ancestor of Saul and of Abner.

Biblical Definition

Abiel was a Benjamite, the head of the house from which both Saul the first king and Abner his captain descended. He was the father of Kish, who was the father of Saul; and the father of Ner, who was the father of Abner (1Sa 9:1; 14:51). Thus from the one house of Abiel sprang both the throne and the sword of the first kingdom: Saul who wore the crown, and Abner who upheld it in war. Abiel himself does nothing in the narrative; he is named only as the root of the family tree. Yet his name is a confession that towers over the history of his descendants: “God is my father.” The house that bore so godly a name rose to the highest place in Israel and then fell under the judgment of God, for Saul forsook the LORD and Abner long resisted His anointed. The name Abiel preached a truth the house failed to keep, that the LORD is the true Father of His people, to be honoured and obeyed above the ties of blood and the ambitions of the throne. Abiel stands at the head of his line as a silent witness that a godly name is no substitute for a faithful heart in the generations that follow.

Webster 1828 Definition

A Benjamite, the common ancestor of Saul and of Abner; his name means “God is my father.”

ABIEL, a Benjamite, the head of the house of Saul and Abner.

He was the father of Kish, the father of Saul (1Sa 9:1).

He was also the father of Ner, the father of Abner (1Sa 14:51).

From his one house sprang both the throne and the captain of the first kingdom.

His name signifies “God is my father.”

Key Scripture

1Sa 9:1 — "Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power."

1Sa 14:51 — "And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel."

1Sa 9:21 — "And Saul answered and said, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou so to me?"

1Ch 8:33 — "And Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal."

Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; his godly name witnesses that lineage cannot supply a faithful heart.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the contrast between Abiel’s name and his house’s end. “God is my father,” the name confessed; yet the line that bore it rose to the throne and fell under judgment, for Saul forsook the LORD. A godly name and a godly ancestry are precious, but they do not pass faith down the generations like an heirloom; each soul must own God as Father for himself.

Abiel, the one root of both Saul and Abner, also teaches that natural unity does not make spiritual unity. The same house gave Israel a king who disobeyed and a captain who long withstood the LORD’s anointed. Blood bound them together, but neither cleaved faithfully to God. The ties of family are a gift, but they are no guarantee of grace; the heart, not the bloodline, must be set on the LORD.

Hebrew Roots

The name joins avi, “my father,” with El, “God,” confessing God as Father.

expand to see more

Abiel — Hebrew Avi’el, “God is my father.”

The element avi means “my father.”

The element El means “God.”

He was father of Kish and of Ner.

He stands at the head of the house of Saul and Abner.

Usage

"Like Abiel’s house, a godly name and ancestry cannot supply a faithful heart to the generations."

"Abiel teaches that natural kinship does not make spiritual unity before God."

"The name “God is my father” must be owned by each soul, not merely inherited."
